title: Which Confluent setup should you price first?

questions.q: What are you setting this up for?

options.label: Learning or testing
options.why: Basic is for development and testing

options.label: A real product, reachable over the public internet
options.why: Standard is the default for public production

options.label: A real product that must stay on a private network
options.why: Enterprise is where private networking lives

questions.q: How does your traffic behave over a day or a week?

options.label: Uneven, it goes up and down
options.why: eCKU clusters scale on their own and idle ones cost nothing

options.label: Lots of logs or events, and a short delay is fine
Steady and large, and I want fixed capacity
options.why: Dedicated is fixed capacity you size yourself

questions.q: Must your app be protected from duplicate or half-finished messages?

options.label: Yes, that would be a problem
options.why: Freight is built for relaxed latency, so check its limits with Confluent before you rely on it where repeats matter

options.label: No, a rare repeat is fine

questions.q: Do you want to see a price before talking to sales?

options.label: Yes, I want a published rate
options.why: the pricing page shows no rate for Dedicated or Tableflow

questions.q: Do you want your streaming data to end up as Iceberg tables in a data lake?

options.label: Yes
options.why: Tableflow is Confluent's own Iceberg path

options.label: No, I just need the streaming itself

basic.name: Basic
basic.summary: A development and testing cluster. The first eCKU is free, then $0.14 per eCKU-hour.
basic.bestWhen: You are learning or testing and want to start at $0.
basic.watchOut: It lists a 99.5% uptime target, lower than the 99.9% or 99.99% on Standard.

standard.name: Standard
standard.summary: Production over the public internet at $0.75 per eCKU-hour.
standard.bestWhen: You run production on public networking and want a published rate.
standard.watchOut: For the 99.99% uptime target you need at least 2 eCKUs, so the floor is double the one-eCKU figure.

enterprise.name: Enterprise
enterprise.summary: Production with private networking at $1.75 to $2.25 per eCKU-hour.
enterprise.watchOut: Clusters scale up to 32 eCKUs, and AWS clusters that use PrivateLink are limited to 10.

freight.name: Freight
freight.summary: For logging and other high-volume work that can live with some delay, at $2.25 per eCKU-hour.
freight.bestWhen: Your traffic is large and latency is relaxed.
freight.watchOut: It does not support share consumers, it is available in select AWS regions, and it has a 2 eCKU minimum.

dedicated.name: Dedicated
dedicated.summary: Fixed, high-throughput capacity that you size yourself in CKUs.
dedicated.bestWhen: Your workload is steady and large, and you are ready to ask for a quote.
dedicated.watchOut: No rate is on the pricing page. You pay for the CKUs whether you use them or not.

tableflow.name: Tableflow
tableflow.summary: Confluent's own path from Kafka topics to Iceberg tables.
tableflow.bestWhen: You want Kafka topics as Iceberg tables inside Confluent.
tableflow.watchOut: There is no Tableflow rate on the pricing page, so you need a quote.
